If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testLang412Right` calls `appendFixedWidthPadRight` with a null argument for the object to append. The implementation of `appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object obj, int width, char padChar)` converts the object to a String by checking if `obj == null`, then using `getNullText()` to get a String representation of null. The code then uses this String to copy characters to an internal buffer. 

The bug report states that appending a null with fixed width causes a NullPointerException if `getNullText()` has not been set. Examining the code confirms this: when `obj == null`, line 1229 in `appendFixedWidthPadRight` does `String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());`. If `getNullText()` returns `null`, then `str` is null, and calling `str.length()` (line 1230) will cause a NullPointerException.

The `getNullText()` method simply returns the value of the private field `nullText`, which by default is presumably null as there is no evidence of initialization. The `setNullText` method allows setting this value, but if not set, it remains null.

Therefore, the root cause of the NullPointerException is that `appendFixedWidthPadRight` does not safely handle the case where `getNullText()` returns null. This aligns with the bug report's description.

Recent bug reports about string length null-safety relate to a similar concept of null-safe handling, but do not directly affect this bug.

In summary: The method `appendFixedWidthPadRight` expects `getNullText()` to return a non-null String, but if it returns null, the method will throw a NullPointerException when it tries to get the length of the string. The method lacks null-safety for the `nullText`.

This explains why the test fails on the given input without nullText set.

Next step: Identify the method(s) to fix this by adding null checks or default null text handling.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
